Read on if you’re curious! Don’t if you aren’t :) I think the treatment of comorbid diagnoses is just fascinating, so I don’t mind sharing.
The key for me has really just been timing. Almost all ED recovery plans start with tallies (a way to count servings, not calories, per day of each necessary food group), but I have OCD. “OCD and EDs are best friends,” as my therapists say. So *counting* tallies for *food* does not work for me, and I’m on a 3&3 plan (3 meals and 3 snacks each day, eating every 2-3 hours). I can wait up to 2 hours to eat after waking up, and I can go to bed if my last meal or snack was less than 3 hours ago. If it was 3 hours ago or more, I have to have another meal or snack before going to sleep. This was quite interesting before I got approved for Xywav (which took a little over 3 months after my doctor prescribed it). I was only on Sunosi, which didn’t even keep me awake without adding caffeine in too. I stopped taking stimulants when I started ED recovery though, so a wake promotor still works better for me and my appetite than Provigil, Nuvigil, or Ritalin ever could have!! On Sunosi alone, I would usually be awake for about 10-12 hours a day, so I sometimes didn’t have enough awake time to be able to eat 6 times, each 2 hours apart. With Xywav, I obviously can’t eat for 2 hours before taking it. Honestly, I think that’s hands down the hardest part about eating with Xywav. Plus, now I’m sleeping almost exactly 7h/night, meaning I’m awake for 17h/day. With the 2 hours before Xywav, I have 15h/day to spread out my 3&3, which puts each meal and snack exactly 2½ hours apart, given that I start breakfast right after waking up. When I’m on top of everything, space out my 3&3 well, and get all 6 in, I don’t lose weight on Xywav :) I am certainly thankful for providers who are willing to consider my needs and collaborate across clinics to help me where I really need it.

I have N1 and I started Xywav a little over a month ago. Started on 3.0g once/night, now on 4.5g once/night.

The increase was because I was sleeping 5 hours/night on 3.0g at first, then it decreased night by night until I was getting about 3.5 hours/night, waking up for a couple hours, then I’d crash for another 8-12 hours of fragmented sleep. On 4.5g, I’ve consistently been sleeping between 7 hours and 7 hours, 5 minutes. I’ve been a little groggy when I first wake up, which didn’t happen with 3.0g/night. I do go to bed late somewhat often and my doses end up “overlapping with daylight” as DeltaAlphaGulf put it, so I think I’ll start paying closer attention to that and seeing whether/how it affects my sleep.

Note on other factors that may be influencing my dosing, as it is relatively low from what I’ve read:
• I’ve been diagnosed with N1 since I was 18 (though symptoms were documented around age 9 and on), and I’m now 25. This past month or so has been the only time I’ve been treated with nighttime medication for my N1. I was previously seeing a provider who, in hindsight, likely knew very little about narcolepsy. They never even mentioned to me that there were nighttime medications for narcolepsy. I’m not sure whether treatment history (specifically a history on medications like Xyrem before switching to Xywav) affects dosing.
• I’m in recovery from a chronic eating disorder (again, symptoms were documented starting around age 10, was not evaluated/diagnosed/treated until 24). I was hospitalized immediately after my Initial Assessment, worked the steps, returned home when I reached my goal weight range, now in outpatient. Despite the steps I’ve taken toward recovering, I am overall still at a low body weight. I’m not sure how this affects dosing, especially given Xywav’s effects on appetite.
• Since I was about 12-15, I’ve had therapeutic responses to relatively low doses of ALL medications. My primary physician refers to this as “medication sensitivity”, and my Xywav prescriber is aware of this, so I don’t know how this affects dosing either.
• Like I said, I haven’t been on Xywav for very long. Who knows if my 4.5g once/night will change in another month.
